evidence.quote: A 31‐year‐old woman from Lima in Peru
arrived at the emergency department

A 31‐year‐old woman from Lima in Peru, presented with a 5‐day history of progressive epigastric pain, fever (38.5°C), early satiety, nausea, and two episodes of vomiting. Physical examination revealed a positive Murphy’s sign and hepatomegaly. Initial imaging and laboratory results raised suspicion of acute cholecystitis, prompting further evaluation prior to surgical intervention.

summary.text: A 31-year-old woman from Lima, Peru presented after five days of progressive severe epigastric pain with fever 38.5°C, early satiety, nausea and two vomiting episodes. Murphy’s sign, hepatomegaly and epigastric tenderness supported initial cholecystitis/obstruction suspicion. Serial liver-function values, cholestatic interpretation and leukocytosis were reported. Ultrasound showed reactive changes, serial wall/size changes and mild intrahepatic duct dilation; MRCP confirmed acalculous cholecystitis and excluded obstruction. Acute HAV serology established secondary AAC; other viral/autoimmune markers were negative. She denied eating outside home or stagnant-source water.

Internal medicine managed the case. Infectious disease recommended antibiotics, but none were administered. First 24-hour IV hydration was followed by tramadol 50 mg, metoclopramide 10 mg and omeprazole 40 mg; subsequent medication routes were unreported. Conservative supportive care/continuous evaluation preceded pain reduction and progressive oral tolerance. Authors reported marker decline within 48 h and inflammation normalization by Day 7, while table AST/ALT peaked Day 2 and bilirubin rose through Day 7. Serial values and literal imaging descriptions remain distinct. After undated discharge, follow-up documented good general condition, normal labs and no known complications/sequelae.
